brief/bd-01.text: What usually happens after a red day?
brief/bd-01.intent: No ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. On the session after a day that closed down, what the price typically did (the usual move and path of that next session).
brief/bd-01.if_asked: SPY. Red day means it closed lower than the day before.
brief/bd-01.also_fine: Red day read as closing below its own open, if that is said.

brief/bd-02.text: When does SPY normally make its high?
brief/bd-02.intent: SPY: at what time of day the session's high is usually made (the distribution of the time of the day's high).
brief/bd-02.if_asked: The time of day of the day's high, over all the history you have.

brief/bd-03.text: Does the first hour tell you anything about the rest of the day?
brief/bd-03.intent: No ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. Whether the direction of the first hour of the session (9:30 to 10:30 New York) goes with the direction of the rest of the session after it.
brief/bd-03.if_asked: SPY. First hour up or down against the rest of the day up or down.

brief/bd-04.text: How far does QQQ usually bounce after a bad open?
brief/bd-04.intent: QQQ: on days that start badly, how far the price typically comes back up. 'A bad open' has no size and could be a gap down or a weak first stretch, so the reading has to be said or asked; no size may be invented.
brief/bd-04.if_asked: A gap down of at least half a percent at the open; the bounce is from the low of the first half hour to the day's high after it.
brief/bd-04.also_fine: Answering with a stated reading that invents no number: for example days QQQ opened below the previous close (any size), and how far it rose from the open to the day's high.

brief/bd-05.intent: As a first message: no ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. Whether Fridays behave differently from the other weekdays (the day's move by weekday, Friday set against the rest).
brief/bd-05.if_asked: SPY, how Fridays compare with the other days of the week.
brief/bd-05.also_fine: Asking 'different in what' is acceptable only if the comparison by weekday is offered as the default.

brief/bd-06.text: Does SPY tend to reverse during lunch?
brief/bd-06.intent: SPY: whether the direction of the morning tends to turn around over the lunch hours (roughly 11:30 to 13:30 New York).
brief/bd-06.if_asked: Whatever it did from the open until lunch, does it go the other way between about 11:30 and 1:30 New York time.
brief/bd-06.also_fine: Asking which hours 'lunch' means, or what move is being reversed, is acceptable if it is one short question.

brief/bd-07.text: What happens after three consecutive down days?
brief/bd-07.intent: No ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. On the session after three or more sessions in a row that closed down, what the price typically did.
brief/bd-07.if_asked: SPY, the day after three down closes in a row.
brief/bd-07.also_fine: Exactly three in a row instead of three or more, if said.

brief/bd-08.text: How often does the market take out yesterday's high?
brief/bd-08.intent: 'The market' with no ticker: the default (SPY), said. How often the price trades above the previous session's high at some point during the session.
brief/bd-08.if_asked: SPY, trading above the previous day's high at any time in the day.

jordan/jd-14.text: Here's one I want to kick around. At 10:30, if SPY is above VWAP, sell a put spread that expires that day: short the 20 delta, long the strike 5 points under it. Two contracts, let it expire. How's that been?
jordan/jd-14.intent: Backtest on SPY options, 2024-01-18 to present: each trading day at 10:30 Eastern time, only if SPY is above its session VWAP, sell 2 same-day-expiration put credit spreads (short the put of about 20 delta, long the put $5 lower) and hold to expiration. Wanted: win rate, average and total profit.
jordan/jd-14.if_asked: Eastern time. VWAP from the 9:30 open. One entry a day, two spreads, held to the close and settled there.

jordan/jd-14.text: what if I don't sit in it all day. take it off once I've kept half the credit, otherwise same thing
jordan/jd-14.intent: Same trade (SPY, 10:30 Eastern time, only when above session VWAP, sell 2 same-day put credit spreads, short about 20 delta, long $5 lower), but close the spread when it can be bought back for 50% of the credit received; if that never happens, hold to expiration.
jordan/jd-14.if_asked: Buy it back when the spread is worth half of what I sold it for. No stop yet.

jordan/jd-14.text: ok and put a stop on it, the losers must be ugly
jordan/jd-14.intent: Same trade with the 50%-of-credit profit target, plus a stop-loss. The stop level, and what it is measured on, are not given. What I meant: also close the spread if SPY falls 0.4% (of SPY's price) below where it was at entry.
jordan/jd-14.if_asked: Out if SPY drops 0.4% from where it was when I sold the spread.

jordan/jd-14.text: let me see the ones that got stopped. the ugliest one in there, did it just go straight down after I got in or what
jordan/jd-14.intent: List the trades from the current version (SPY, 10:30 Eastern time, above VWAP, 2 same-day put credit spreads, short about 20 delta and long $5 lower, profit target at 50% of the credit, stop when SPY is 0.4% below its entry price) that were closed by the stop, with date, credit received, exit price and loss; and for the largest loss among them, describe what SPY did after the 10:30 entry that day.
jordan/jd-14.if_asked: Just the stopped-out trades with the date and what each lost, and for the biggest loser what SPY did after 10:30 that day.

jordan/jd-14.text: now make it a real plan. 30k account, take it at 10:30, noon and 1:30 whenever it's above VWAP at that time, risk 3% of the account on each one, and I'm done for the day once I've lost $1,500. No compounding, keep it off the 30k.
jordan/jd-14.intent: SPY same-day-expiration put credit spreads (short about 20 delta, long $5 lower) entered at 10:30, 12:00 and 13:30 Eastern time, each only if SPY is above its session VWAP at that time, 2024-01-18 to present. Each is closed at 50% of the credit received (profit) or when SPY is 0.4% below its price at that entry (stop), otherwise held to expiration. Starting account $30,000, each trade sized so its maximum loss is about 3% of $30,000 ($900) without reinvesting gains, and no new trades that day once the day's losses reach $1,500.
jordan/jd-14.if_asked: Up to three entries a day. $900 at risk on each, fixed, based on the most the spread can lose. Stop trading for the day at $1,500 of losses. Same target and stop as before.
jordan/jd-14.also_fine: Sizing the $900 against the expected loss at the stop instead of the spread's full maximum loss, if stated.

jordan/jd-14.text: run that on the Qs and put it next to the SPY numbers
jordan/jd-14.intent: The same plan on QQQ instead of SPY, shown side by side with the SPY result: same-day put credit spreads (short about 20 delta, long $5 lower) at 10:30, 12:00 and 13:30 Eastern time when QQQ is above its session VWAP, closed at 50% of the credit or when QQQ is 0.4% below its entry price, otherwise held to expiration. $30,000 account, about $900 maximum loss per trade, no reinvesting, no new trades after $1,500 of losses in a day, 2024-01-18 to present.
jordan/jd-14.if_asked: Everything the same, just QQQ, still 5 wide. Then both results together.
